name: Question 7
worked_solution:
To integrate a vector-valued function, we integrate each component separately:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int ⟨{e}^{t},\,10\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t-\frac{\pi }{6})⟩\text{d}t=⟨\int {e}^{t}\,\text{d}t,\,\int 10\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t-\frac{\pi }{6})\,\text{d}t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

- For $x(t)={e}^{t},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x(t)\,\text{d}t=\int {e}^{t}\text{d}t={e}^{t}+{c}_{1}.\end{aligned}
$$

- For $y(t)=10\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t-\frac{\pi }{6}),$ we calculate its integral using substitution. So, we let $u=2t-\frac{\pi }{6}.$ Then

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t}=2\,⟹\,\text{d}t=\frac{1}{2}\text{d}u.
$$

Therefore,  we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int y(t)\,\text{d}t & =\int 10\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t-\frac{\pi }{6})\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int 10\operatorname{cos}⁡u\cdot \frac{1}{2}\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{10}{2}\int \operatorname{cos}⁡u\,\text{d}u \\  & =5(\operatorname{sin}⁡u)+{c}_{2} \\  & =5\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t-\frac{\pi }{6})+{c}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int ⟨{e}^{t},\,10\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t-\frac{\pi }{6})⟩\text{d}t & =⟨{e}^{t}+{c}_{1},\,5\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t-\frac{\pi }{6})+{c}_{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨{e}^{t},\,5\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t-\frac{\pi }{6})⟩+⟨{c}_{1},\,{c}_{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨{e}^{t},\,5\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t-\frac{\pi }{6})⟩+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 7
?

Find ∫⟨et,10cos⁡(2t−π6)⟩dt.

a
⟨et,5sin⁡(2t)⟩+C
b
⟨et,5sin⁡(2t−π6)⟩+C
c
⟨et−1,sin⁡(t−π6)⟩+C
d
⟨et−1,5sin⁡(2t−π6)⟩+C
e
⟨e5t,5cos⁡(t−π2)⟩+C
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

To integrate a vector-valued function, we integrate each component separately:

∫⟨et,10cos⁡(2t−π6)⟩dt=⟨∫etdt,∫10cos⁡(2t−π6)dt⟩.

  • For x(t)=et, we have ∫x(t)dt=∫etdt=et+c1.

  • For y(t)=10cos⁡(2t−π6), we calculate its integral using substitution. So, we let u=2t−π6. Then
    dudt=2⟹dt=12du. Therefore, we have ∫y(t)dt=∫10cos⁡(2t−π6)dt=∫10cos⁡u⋅12du=102∫cos⁡udu=5(sin⁡u)+c2=5sin⁡(2t−π6)+c2.

Finally, we get

∫⟨et,10cos⁡(2t−π6)⟩dt=⟨et+c1,5sin⁡(2t−π6)+c2⟩=⟨et,5sin⁡(2t−π6)⟩+⟨c1,c2⟩=⟨et,5sin⁡(2t−π6)⟩+C.
